subtitle: From Aurangzeb’s Court to a Vanished King

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle mid-shot set against the massive walls of Agra Fort at dusk
panels.action: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj stands in simple but dignified attire, hands loosely bound by a thin chain, guards silhouetted behind him as the looming red sandstone of Agra Fort glows under a fading sky.

dialogue.text: In 1666, within Aurangzeb’s own stronghold at Agra, Shivaji—captive king of the Deccan—simply vanished, leaving court historians scrambling to explain how an imprisoned rebel defied an empire.

i18n.hi: १६६६ में, आगरा के औरंगज़ेब क़िले में, दक्कन का क़ैदी राजा शिवाजी अचानक ओझल हो गया, और दरबारी इतिहासकार सिर पकड़कर सोचते रह गए कि बंद बग़ावत ने सल्तनत को कैसे ललकार दिया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide shot of a Mughal highway caravan moving toward a distant city
panels.action: Shivaji rides in a guarded palanquin along the royal road, Mughal horsemen flanking him, dust rising as the red silhouette of Agra and its fort appears faintly on the horizon.

dialogue.text: That summer, the Mughal road to Agra shimmered in the heat as Shivaji, summoned by Aurangzeb and escorted by imperial troops, left the Deccan to enter the lion’s den.

i18n.hi: उस गर्मी, औरंगज़ेब के बुलावे पर, बादशाही सिपाहियों से घिरे शिवाजी दक्कन से चले, तपती सड़क पार कर शेर की माँद में दाख़िल होने।

panels.shot: slow push-in from wide to medium on Shivaji inside the palanquin
panels.action: Inside the palanquin, Shivaji sits cross‑legged, composed yet alert, fingers tracing a rough map in the dust on the floor as the palanquin’s curtains sway with each jolt.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: To bow in court… yet guard the swarajya in my mind.

i18n.hi: दरबार में सिर झुकाऊँ… पर मन में स्वराज्य नहीं झुकने दूँ।

panels.shot: epic interior wide of Aurangzeb’s birthday durbar from behind Shivaji’s shoulder
panels.action: Shivaji stands in the crowded Agra audience hall, seen from behind, as rows of Mughal nobles in jeweled robes line the carpeted hall and Aurangzeb sits distant on a raised throne beneath a canopy.

dialogue.text: On 12 May 1666, at Aurangzeb’s grand birthday durbar, the Maratha leader walked into a hall of brocade and suspicion, ranked below Afghan chiefs he had fought against.

i18n.hi: १२ मई १६६६ को, औरंगज़ेब के शाही सालाना दरबार में, मराठा सरदार रेशमी शानो–शौक़ और शक के बीच उस हॉल में दाख़िल हुआ, अफ़ग़ान सरदारों से नीचे बिठाया गया जिनसे वो लड़ चुका था।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Shivaji’s face, with the Mughal ranks blurred behind
panels.action: Shivaji’s face is calm but tightened, eyes focused, as behind him blurred figures of high-ranking nobles take places ahead of him in the ceremonial line.

dialogue.text: The Akhbarat notes only his presence; later bakhars add his anger at being slighted. What is certain is that the rebel of the Western Ghats felt himself diminished amid imperial choreographies.

i18n.hi: अख़बारात बस उसकी मौजूदगी का ज़िक्र करते हैं; बाद की बख़रें उसकी ठेस खाई झल्लाहट जोड़ देती हैं। इतना पक्का है कि पश्चिमी घाट का यह बाग़ी शहंशाही नाच में खुद को छोटा महसूस कर रहा था।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Shivaji turning his back on the throne and walking away
panels.action: Shivaji turns from the throne and strides toward the exit past startled courtiers, his shoulders straight, a few hands half‑raised as if to stop him but held back by the decorum of the hall.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: I came as a servant of peace, not as a pawn in insult.

i18n.hi: मैं सुलह का ख़ादिम बनकर आया हूँ, तमाशे की बेइज़्ज़ती नहीं।

panels.shot: low-angle long shot of Agra Fort’s exterior with soldiers closing a gate
panels.action: Massive wooden gates of an Agra residence compound swing shut as Mughal soldiers take positions, while inside the gateway Shivaji is seen being led to quarters within high enclosing walls.

dialogue.text: The Alamgirnama and court bulletins grow sparse, but they agree: after that day’s affront, Shivaji was placed under guard in Agra, his movements watched, his future in Aurangzeb’s hands.

i18n.hi: आलमगीरनामा और दरबारी एलान कम होते जाते हैं, पर मानते हैं: उस दिन की तौहीन के बाद, शिवाजी को आगरा में नज़रबंद कर दिया गया, हर हरक़त पर पहरा, उसकी तक़दीर औरंगज़ेब के हाथों में।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot of Shivaji seated in a modest chamber with a barred window
panels.action: In a plain Mughal chamber, Shivaji sits near a small barred window, a few attendants nearby; outside, a guard’s shadow cuts across the lattice as evening light falls in slanting beams.

dialogue.text: It was not a dank dungeon but a guarded residence, placed formally under the supervision of Raja Ram Singh, son of Jai Singh, who now walked a tightrope between imperial loyalty and Rajput honor.

i18n.hi: यह सीलन भरी कालकोठरी नहीं, पहरेदारों से घिरा मकान था, जिसे औपचारिक तौर पर राजा रामसिंह, जयसिंह के बेटे, के सुपुर्द किया गया, जो अब वफ़ादारी और राजपूताना आन के बीच रस्सी पर चल रहा था।

panels.shot: two-shot from inside the room toward the door, hinting at Ram Singh outside
panels.action: Through the half‑open door, the silhouette of a Rajput noble stands respectfully at a distance as Shivaji, inside, inclines his head slightly, the space between them charged with unspoken politics.

dialogue.text: Jai Singh, who had negotiated the 1665 treaty, had staked his word on Shivaji’s safety. His son Ram Singh could not simply let the Maratha go, yet could not bear an ignoble fate for his charge.

i18n.hi: १६६५ की सुलह कराने वाले जयसिंह ने शिवाजी की हिफ़ाज़त पर अपनी ज़मानत रख दी थी। उसका बेटा रामसिंह न मराठा को खुले छोड़ सकता था, न अपने मेहमान की बेइज़्ज़त मौत बर्दाश्त।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the chamber with Shivaji’s young son nearby
panels.action: Shivaji sits on a simple rug with a young boy beside him, perhaps his son, as he gestures softly, while in a dark corner a sentry’s outline reminds us of the constant surveillance.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: Chains on the body are one thing. Chains on the will, another.

i18n.hi: शरीर की ज़ंजीरें और हैं, इरादे की ज़ंजीरें और।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot of days passing, shown by changing light through the same window
panels.action: Three overlapping images of the same room show Shivaji pacing, then sitting in meditation, then quietly speaking with an attendant, while the light through the lattice shifts from dawn to noon to dusk.

dialogue.text: Weeks lengthened. The Akhbarat records petitions and counter‑petitions at court—questions of rank, jagirs, and trust—while in that guarded house Shivaji measured time in footsteps and plans.

i18n.hi: हफ़्ते महीनों में बदल गए। अख़बारात में रुतबे, जागीर और यक़ीन पर अर्जी–पेशियाँ दर्ज रहीं, और उस पहरे वाले घर में शिवाजी ने क़दम गिन–गिनकर योजना बुननी शुरू कर दी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Shivaji speaking quietly to a trusted attendant
panels.action: Shivaji leans close to a bearded attendant, his face in shadow, hand resting on the man’s arm as he whispers, while beyond them a barred doorway hints at the listening ears of the empire.

dialogue.text: Later historians like Stewart Gordon argue that money, persuasion, or disguise likely loosened those bars. The chronicles fall silent here, their ink stopping where the risk for living officials began.

i18n.hi: बाद के इतिहासकार, जैसे स्टीवर्ट गॉर्डन, मानते हैं कि रुपया, रिआयत या भेष ने सलाखें ढीली कीं। यहाँ तवारीख़ चुप हो जाती हैं, जहाँ आगे लिखना ज़िंदा अमीरों के लिए ख़तरा था।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot on large baskets of sweets being carried out of a courtyard
panels.action: Strong porters heft two oversized, lidded baskets as they exit a courtyard, a faint suggestion of guards watching with bored expressions, while the walls frame a narrow slice of sky.

dialogue.text: The Sabhasad Bakhar, written later in the Maratha camp, tells it differently: Shivaji and his son hidden in baskets of sweets, carried past unsuspecting guards under the cover of pious offerings.

i18n.hi: सभासद बख़र, जो बाद में मराठा डेरों में लिखी गई, अलग कहती है: शिवाजी और उनके बेटे को मिठाइयों की टोकरी में छिपाकर, धर्म–दान के बहाने नासमझ पहरेदारों के सामने से निकाल दिया गया।

panels.shot: tight, almost claustrophobic close-up inside a dark wicker basket
panels.action: From within a cramped wicker basket, faint light seeping through gaps, Shivaji’s calm eyes peer through the weave as the basket tilts, hinting at motion and the muffled world beyond.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: If legend preserves courage, let the form of the tale be its own armor.

i18n.hi: अगर दंतकथा हौसला बचाती है, तो उसकी शक्ल ही उसकी ढाल रहे।

panels.shot: sharp cut to an alternative image: Shivaji cloaked in plain clothes among porters
panels.action: Shivaji, dressed as a modest household retainer with a turban pulled low, walks calmly among other workers through a side gate, his posture unremarkable as wary guards glance only briefly at the group.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars counter that bribed guards or quiet disguise are more plausible than baskets. Between these frames—one of romance, one of bureaucracy—lies the space where history and memory wrestle.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान कहते हैं, रिश्वतख़ोर पहरेदार या खामोश भेषदारी, टोकरियों से ज़्यादा मुमकिन हैं। इन्हीं दो तस्वीरों के बीच—एक रुमान, एक दफ़्तरी—वही जद्दोजहद है जहाँ इतिहास और यादें कुश्ती लड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide night-time shot of a small group slipping through a city lane away from Agra’s glow
panels.action: Under a moonlit sky, Shivaji and a handful of companions move quickly down a narrow lane, the distant bulk of Agra Fort fading behind them as the open countryside begins beyond the last houses.

dialogue.text: What is certain is that by mid‑August 1666, Shivaji had slipped beyond Agra’s grasp. The imperial bulletins note the fact of his disappearance with terse embarrassment, not the manner of his flight.

i18n.hi: इतना तय है कि १६६६ के अगस्त के बीच तक, शिवाजी आगरा की पकड़ से फिसल चुके थे। शाही अख़बारात ने बस उनकी गुमशुदगी दर्ज की, उड़ते–उड़ते, पर भागने का तरीका नहीं।

panels.shot: broad, atmospheric wide of the North Indian plain with distant temple spires and trees
panels.action: A dusty road winds across the North Indian plain past groves of trees and distant temple spires, tiny figures on the path suggesting travelers moving steadily away from the unseen imperial city.

dialogue.text: Traditions place his path through the sacred landscapes of north India, perhaps Mathura’s environs, but the precise route dissolves into rumor; only the outcome remains sharp—Shivaji reached the Deccan alive.

i18n.hi: रिवायतें उनके क़दम उत्तर भारत की पवित्र धरती, शायद मथुरा के आस–पास, पर रखती हैं, पर असल रास्ता अफ़वाहों में घुल जाता है; नतीजा साफ़ है—शिवाजी ज़िंदा दक्कन लौट पहुँचे।

panels.shot: interior wide of the Mughal court, focused on Aurangzeb seated with advisors
panels.action: Aurangzeb sits stern on his throne as courtiers and scribes murmur below, some heads bowed low, a scribe’s hand poised above a page, capturing the news of the vanished Maratha rebel.

dialogue.text: In Agra, the court scrambled. Orders flew, explanations were crafted, and blame veered toward Ram Singh, even as his defenders argued that a king cannot be caged like a petty bandit without cost.

i18n.hi: आगरा में दरबार घबरा उठा। हुक्म बरसने लगे, सफ़ाइयाँ गढ़ी गईं, इल्ज़ाम रामसिंह पर टिकाया गया, जबकि उसके हामी कहते रहे कि राजा को सस्ते डाकू की तरह पिंजरे में बंद करना आख़िर मुफ़्त नहीं पड़ता।

panels.shot: heroic low-angle wide of Shivaji on a Deccan hilltop looking westward
panels.action: On a rugged Deccan hilltop, Shivaji stands silhouetted against dawn, cloak stirred by the wind, forts and dark valleys stretching behind him, his gaze fixed toward a horizon that now lies beyond Mughal reach.

dialogue.text: From this vanishing at Agra grew a legend of baskets and bribes, but the deeper truth endures: when power believed it had closed every door, Shivaji found a crack, and turned captivity into a passage for his people’s future.

i18n.hi: आगरा की इस ग़ायबी से टोकरियों और रिश्वत की दंतकथा तो बनी, पर गहरी सच्चाई यही रही: जब ताक़त को लगा सारी राहें उसने बंद कर दीं, शिवाजी ने एक दरार खोज ली, और कैद को अपनी कौम के भविष्य की राह बना दिया।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Aurangzeb’s Court to a Vanished King
subtitle_i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब की दरबार से ग़ायब बादशाह तक
